title: One ticket a week until you win
hook: Jackpot odds are 1 in 292 million. How long would a ticket every week take to win?

knows: '1 in a million' means very unlikely
doesNotKnow: how big 1 in 292 million is in human time
that an expected wait is an average, not a promise

misconception: Lottery wins are unlikely per ticket, but a lifetime of weekly tickets gives a real chance.
objective: The learner can say that weekly tickets would take about 5.6 million years to expect one jackpot, and that a lifetime of tickets (about 4,200) gives roughly a 0.0014% chance.
keyState: Reached 80 years (4,174 tickets, 0.0014% chance, no win) and the expected wait (5.6 million years, 63% chance by then).

claims.text: The jackpot odds are 1 in 292,201,338 per ticket.
claims.source: Powerball jackpot odds since October 2015: C(69,5) x 26 = 11,238,513 x 26 = 292,201,338 (recomputed in node). Operator's published odds: powerball.com 'Prizes and Odds'. The lesson uses it as 'a jackpot', no other Powerball rule.

claims.text: One ticket a week for 1, 10, 80, 1,000 and 100,000 years is 52, 522, 4,174, 52,179 and 5,217,857 tickets.
claims.source: tickets(y) = round(y x 365.25/7) with 52.18 weeks per year (model.ts).

claims.text: To expect one win takes 292,201,338 weekly tickets, about 5.6 million years.
claims.source: Mean of a geometric wait = 1/p = 292,201,338 weeks; / 52.1786 = 5,600,026 years (EXPECTED_YEARS in model.ts). Options 5,600 / 56,000 / 5.6 million years are this value /1000, /100 and x1.

claims.text: The chance of at least one jackpot is 0.0014% over an 80-year lifetime of weekly tickets, 0.018% over 1,000 years, 1.8% over 100,000 years and 63% by the expected wait.
claims.source: chanceBy(t) = 1 - (1 - 1/292,201,338)^t in model.ts: t = 4,174 gives 1.43e-5; 52,179 gives 1.79e-4; 5,217,857 gives 0.0177; 292,201,338 gives 1 - 1/e = 0.632. 1 and 10 years: 1.8e-5% and 1.8e-4%. At this run's first win (343,820,670 tickets, 6.6 million years) the readout shows 69%.

claims.text: In the stage's run, the first win came at about 6.6 million years, later than the expected wait; before that it had 0 wins at every span.
claims.source: firstWinWeek() in model.ts: one mulberry32 draw, seed 1969, untuned (the first seed tried), inverted through the geometric distribution: week 343,820,670 = 6,589,308 years (1.18x the mean). Over seeds 1-1000 the first win / expected wait had median 0.68, middle 95% 0.023-3.6, and 64% of runs won before the expected wait; no seed won within 80 years.

claims.text: An 80-year lifetime is under 0.002% of the 5.6-million-year expected wait.
claims.source: 80 / 5,600,026 = 1.4e-5 (the timeline's 'a lifetime' mark vs the expected-wait span; log axis, each tick 10x).

recall.question: A lottery has odds of 1 in 10 million per ticket. Playing once a week, roughly how long until you would expect a win?
recall.why: 10 million weekly tickets at 52 a year is about 190,000 years. Divide the odds by tickets per year; a lifetime is only about 4,000 tickets.
